jobs.prompt:
feat(cpp): follower mode so a side-by-side gateway never rotates the shared upstream subscription login

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). The owner will run it for a week on the SAME host as the production gateway, on another port, with a COPY of the production state. Both gateways then hold the same upstream subscription logins (the Codex/ChatGPT OAuth pool; also the Antigravity/Gemini CLI state if that provider is enabled). Those logins use ROTATING refresh tokens: when one gateway refreshes, the provider invalidates the other gateway's copy, which then answers 401 until a human repairs it (the code documents this: see the Codex auth refresh and auth repair modules and their `refresh_token_reused` handling). The production gateway must stay healthy as the emergency fallback, so the test gateway must never be the one that refreshes. Read `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CUTOVER.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test>`), `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md`. Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body (short, plain language, with the operator instructions).

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev` gives a toolchain that builds this tree (the CI workflow shows the exact package list and how it builds the pinned SQLite: do the same). The environment has `CCACHE_DIR` set to a directory that is restored before and saved after your job; `ccache` is installed.


RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Tests use local mocks only: no real provider traffic.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each step, keep a checklist in `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-follower-mode-20261120.md`, read it and `git log` first after a restart. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes.
- Do not delete or weaken tests. Default behaviour (switch unset) must be byte-for-byte what it is today.

TASK
1. Map every place the gateway can change a shared upstream credential or call an OAuth token endpoint: Codex access-token refresh (including the refresh lease, compare-and-set of the pool, proactive refresh before expiry, refresh on 401), auth repair/adoption, account pool mutation by admin routes, Codex CLI/supervisor paths that may refresh on their own, and the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) which keeps its own OAuth state on disk. Write the map into the report.
2. Add ONE operator switch, `UOS_GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_AUTH_FOLLOWER=1` (exactly `1` enables; documented in the environment table of `docs/RUNTIME.md`). When enabled: the gateway NEVER calls a token endpoint and never writes a refreshed or rotated credential for a shared subscription login; a request that would need a refresh fails for that account the way an unavailable account does today (existing failover to other accounts/providers and the existing client-visible error apply) and the terminal log records a distinct reason such as `upstream_auth_follower_stale`; admin routes that would mutate the shared pool are refused with a clear 409-style error naming the switch; read-only validation (the usage probe the repair module already uses) is still allowed. For the Antigravity CLI: in follower mode do not enable the provider at all (log why), because the CLI refreshes its own login outside the gateway's control. API-key providers are unaffected.
3. Staleness handling: when the leader refreshes, the follower's copy goes stale. Provide the supported way to pick up the leader's new credentials WITHOUT the follower ever refreshing: an operator command or documented procedure that imports the Codex auth pool from another gateway state directory (the leader's stopped-consistent copy) into the follower's state while the follower is stopped, touching only the auth pool records (reuse the existing auth repair/adoption code paths and their validation; do not copy unrelated data). Add this to `docs/CUTOVER.md` as "Running side by side on one host" with the exact steps and the warning that follower mode must be removed before the follower becomes the only gateway.
4. `/health` (or the existing diagnostics route) must show that follower mode is on and how long until the earliest shared access token expires (time only, never token material), so the operator sees staleness coming.
5. Tests with mock token endpoints and scripted upstreams: follower with an expired access token makes zero token-endpoint calls and fails over or errors as specified; follower on upstream 401 does not refresh; default mode still refreshes exactly as before (existing tests unchanged and passing); admin pool mutation refused in follower mode; the import procedure adopts a newer credential and rejects a broken one; Gemini provider stays disabled in follower mode even when its own opt-in is set. Release and `--config asan`, plus the existing Codex auth, routing and admin tests.

DONE WHEN
With the switch on there is no code path that reaches a token endpoint or writes a rotated shared credential (shown by the map and tests), the default is unchanged, the import procedure works, and the documents describe the side-by-side setup.
